title: ScoredReplayRun
description: Scored Postgame Replay milestone: the aggregate scoring report for one already-completed ReplayRun's ReplayResults, joined against canonical postgame settlement/CLV/bet evidence once available. Research-only -- never read by the production pipeline, never written in place of or over a ReplayRun. See docs/SCORED_REPLAY.md.

scoredReplayRunId.description: sha1('scored_replay_run', replayRunId, scoringFrameworkVersion) -- see lib/edgelab/ids.py:build_scored_replay_run_id. Deterministic over (replayRunId, scoringFrameworkVersion) ONLY, deliberately not over settlement/CLV/bet content, so a later corrected settlement re-derives the SAME id and updates this record's content in place rather than orphaning a stale one.

replayRunId.description: The ReplayRun this scores. That run's own file (data/edgelab/replay_runs/<replayRunId>/*) is never modified by this record's existence.

snapshotId.description: Copied verbatim from the scored ReplayRun's own snapshotId.

scoringFrameworkVersion.description: Version of this scoring layer itself (lib.edgelab.scored_replay.SCORING_FRAMEWORK_VERSION) -- distinct from replayFrameworkVersion, since scoring logic can change independent of the replay engine it reads.

limitationReasons.description: Union of the source ReplayRun's own limitationReasons plus any scoring-specific gap, e.g. WAGER_LINKAGE_UNAVAILABLE when the linked postgame settlement snapshot could not be located.

summary.description: aggregate_scored_results() over this run's own ScoredReplayResults. Null only when the run had zero markets (never a fabricated all-zero report).

realizedPnl.description: Computed exclusively from CONFIRMED_BET rows (a genuine, non-CANCELLED PlacedBet record linked via canonical settlement.betId) -- never from a recommendation or a replayed/hypothetical stake.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 over this run's content-only serialization plus every ScoredReplayResult's content-only serialization (timestamps/provenance excluded). write_scored_replay_outputs compares this against any existing on-disk record to distinguish a true no-op rerun from a genuine content update (e.g. a corrected settlement).
